metadata.title: Do They Actually Like Me?
metadata.description: Read the pattern behind mixed signals, quiet interest, inconsistent effort, and the uncertainty that makes every small cue feel important.
metadata.description_zh: 看清曖昧訊號、安靜的在乎、忽冷忽熱的投入，以及為甚麼一個小細節都會令你開始猜。

H1.label: Consistent interest
H1.definition: Their behavior repeatedly shows voluntary interest, follow-through, curiosity, and a reliable place for the customer in their life.
H1.signals: Initiates and follows through; remembers details; makes realistic plans; reconnects after space; behavior and words broadly match.
H1.counter: Warm moments are repeatedly followed by withdrawal, vague plans, or little voluntary investment.

H2.label: Inconsistent investment
H2.definition: Interest may be present, but investment fluctuates enough that the relationship is difficult to rely on.
H2.signals: Hot-cold contact; vague future talk; plans without follow-through; interest appears mainly when convenient or when the customer pulls away.
H2.counter: Low-frequency contact is paired with dependable planning, follow-through, and clear re-engagement.

H3.label: Low-expression style
H3.definition: They may care consistently but show it through quieter, practical, or slower forms of attention rather than frequent verbal or digital signals.
H3.signals: Sparse texting but reliable actions; reserved public style; practical care; needs more solo time yet communicates boundaries and returns.
H3.counter: Low expression is also paired with low effort, unclear intentions, and repeated failure to follow through.

H4.label: Ambiguity amplification
H4.definition: The available evidence is mixed or limited, while uncertainty makes small signals carry more meaning than the broader pattern supports.
H4.signals: Monitoring reply timing, likes, wording, or comparison cues; one-off changes feel highly diagnostic; reassurance quickly becomes necessary.
H4.counter: Judgments remain anchored in repeated behavior, direct conversations, and longer-term patterns rather than isolated cues.

stopping.High Evidence Band: Lead margin >=7 AND strong-primary answers >= 6 AND evidence domains >= 5
stopping.Moderate Evidence Band: Lead margin 4–6 AND minimum strong-primary/domain/stability criteria all met
stopping.Mixed / Low Evidence Band: Lead margin <4 at max, or top two remain materially supported
stopping.Deterministic Stop Rule: Before 20: continue. At/after 20: stop only if lead margin >=4, strong-primary answers >= 5, distinct positive-evidence domains >= 5, and same primary has remained #1 for last 3 answered questions. Otherwise continue until 30. At max, if margin <4 return mixed profile; never arbitrary tie-break.
stopping.Calibration Status: Production-authoring thresholds copied from approved V3.1 Deep/Standard profile; MUST pass persona simulation before RELEASE_REVIEW

resultBlueprints.Headline EN: Their interest looks more consistent than confusing.
resultBlueprints.Headline 中文: 比起「猜不透」，對方的興趣其實更像是穩定而有跡可尋。
resultBlueprints.We're With You EN: When the signals are steady but not dramatic, it can still be surprisingly hard to trust what is right in front of you. Across your answers, the recurring clues were that they keep initiating and following through instead of leaving all the momentum to you and that their plans become specific and their actions broadly match what they say. Taken together, the pattern is less about one dramatic moment and more about this: their interest is showing up as a repeated pattern of voluntary effort, follow-through and real curiosity about you.
resultBlueprints.站在你這邊 中文: 當對方的訊號其實算穩定，只是沒有很戲劇化時，反而很容易懷疑自己是不是看得太樂觀。較一致的線索包括「對方會主動，也會把說過的安排做到，而不是一直由你推動關係」，以及「計劃會變得具體，而且說過的話大致跟行動一致」。這些情況放在一起，較接近的解讀是：對方的興趣不是只靠一兩個甜蜜時刻，而是反覆出現在主動、跟進和真正想了解你這些行動上。
resultBlueprints.Deeper Pattern EN: Underneath the question “do they like me?” is a second question: which signals deserve your trust. In your answers, the line that kept returning was this: their interest is showing up as a repeated pattern of voluntary effort, follow-through and real curiosity about you. Another explanation can still be present; what matters is whether this same line keeps appearing across different situations rather than whether every single moment looks perfect.

resultBlueprints.Professional View EN: The safest way to read interest is to move from guessing intention to tracking repeated behaviour: they remember details, make room for you, and reconnect reliably after busy periods. This reading becomes weaker if warm moments keep being followed by vague plans, withdrawal or very little voluntary effort. So take this as the explanation that best fits your answers right now, not proof of what another person privately feels.

resultBlueprints.Evidence Guidance EN: The answers carrying the most weight are the ones where they keep initiating and following through instead of leaving all the momentum to you, their plans become specific and their actions broadly match what they say, or they remember details, make room for you, and reconnect reliably after busy periods. metadata.description: Separate missing the person from missing validation, familiarity, or the closure you never really got.
metadata.description_zh: 分清楚你想念的是這個人、被重視的感覺、熟悉的生活，還是一直沒有真正完結的那一頁。

H1.label: Missing the person
H1.definition: What is hard to release is the actual person and the specific connection, not only the role they played.
H1.signals: Misses their mind, humor, values, ordinary presence, and a relationship that still seems meaningful even without attention or status.
H1.counter: Longing drops sharply when validation, routine, or hope of reunion is removed.

H2.label: Missing validation
H2.definition: A large part of the longing comes from missing how wanted, attractive, important, or chosen the relationship made the customer feel.
H2.signals: Replays compliments; wants them to regret leaving; jealousy centers on replacement; attention from someone new noticeably reduces the pull.
H2.counter: The bond still feels deeply missed even when ego, competition, and being wanted are taken out of the picture.

H3.label: Missing familiarity
H3.definition: The loss is strongly tied to routine, shared identity, places, rituals, mutual friends, and the structure of everyday life.
H3.signals: Misses rituals and shared spaces; identity feels disrupted; ordinary routines trigger grief more than romantic memories.
H3.counter: The customer can rebuild routines but still specifically longs for the person or unresolved relationship.

H4.label: Unfinished ending
H4.label_zh: 這段關係仍未真正完結
H4.definition: Ambiguity, unanswered questions, imagined future repair, or a lack of closure keeps the relationship psychologically open.
H4.signals: Rechecks old messages; waits for contact; imagines one final conversation; longing intensifies around unanswered 'what if' questions.
H4.counter: Even with a clear final ending and no possibility of reunion, the same longing remains.

stopping.High Evidence Band: Lead margin >=7 AND strong-primary answers >= 6 AND evidence domains >= 5
stopping.Moderate Evidence Band: Lead margin 4–6 AND minimum strong-primary/domain/stability criteria all met
stopping.Mixed / Low Evidence Band: Lead margin <4 at max, or top two remain materially supported
stopping.Deterministic Stop Rule: Before 20: continue. At/after 20: stop only if lead margin >=4, strong-primary answers >= 5, distinct positive-evidence domains >= 5, and same primary has remained #1 for last 3 answered questions. Otherwise continue until 30. At max, if margin <4 return mixed profile; never arbitrary tie-break.

metadata.title: Are My Standards Unreasonable?
metadata.description: Test whether you are asking for healthy basics, facing a genuine mismatch, carrying too much of the relationship, or needing more reassurance than the relationship can sustainably provide.
metadata.description_zh: 看看你的需要其實很合理、只是彼此偏好不同，還是你已經在一段不對等的關係裡不斷降低標準。

H1.label: Healthy core needs
H1.definition: The customer is mainly asking for baseline respect, consistency, honesty, boundaries, and enough emotional engagement for a relationship to function.
H1.signals: Needs reciprocity, respectful conflict, clear boundaries, basic reliability, and honest expectations.
H1.counter: The expectation mainly concerns constant availability, mind-reading, or proof that exceeds the actual agreement.

H2.label: Preference mismatch
H2.definition: Neither person is necessarily wrong; they may simply want different levels of contact, affection, social visibility, independence, or relationship structure.
H2.signals: Different but internally consistent preferences; both sides can explain needs; mismatch persists without one person clearly underinvesting.
H2.counter: One person repeatedly agrees to the standard but does not follow through, or dismisses the other's needs.

H3.label: Unequal reciprocity
H3.definition: The customer may be labeling ordinary needs as 'too much' because they are carrying more initiative, repair, planning, or support than the other person.
H3.signals: One-sided planning; repeated cancellations; support is not returned; customer supplies most relationship momentum.
H3.counter: Effort is broadly mutual and the conflict is mainly about preferred style or reassurance frequency.

H4.label: High reassurance expectations
H4.definition: Some expectations are driven by a strong need for frequent confirmation, rapid response, or continuous proof that the relationship is secure.

resultBlueprints.We're With You EN: Wondering whether you are 'too much' often happens after your needs have been questioned for long enough. Across your answers, the recurring clues were that you are asking for basic reliability rather than constant availability and that you expect honest communication and respectful conflict, not mind-reading. Taken together, the pattern is less about one dramatic moment and more about this: most of what you are asking for looks like the basic conditions that let a relationship function: respect, honesty, consistency and workable boundaries.

resultBlueprints.Deeper Pattern EN: The deeper issue is not whether you are demanding or easygoing; it is what kind of relationship standard your answers keep protecting. Across the different situations, one kind of need kept standing out: most of what you are asking for looks like the basic conditions that let a relationship function: respect, honesty, consistency and workable boundaries. Another explanation may still matter, so keep asking whether the same need or mismatch appears across different situations instead of judging yourself from one request.

resultBlueprints.Professional View EN: In real life, a fair standard is easier to judge by reciprocity, agreements, and repeated follow-through than by whether someone calls you “too much”: your boundaries leave room for both people to have autonomy. This reading becomes weaker if the expectation mainly asks for constant access, mind-reading or proof beyond what the relationship actually agreed. Treat this as a way to test the pattern in your relationship, not as a diagnosis of you or proof that one person's preferences are universally right.

metadata.title_zh: 這只是低潮，還是我們正在漸行漸遠？
metadata.description: Look at whether the distance is coming from temporary pressure, a repairable communication problem, emotional disengagement, or a deeper difference in where the relationship is going.
metadata.description_zh: 分清楚你們只是被壓力拖進低潮，還是溝通、情感投入或未來方向真的開始出現裂縫。

H1.label: External strain
H1.definition: The relationship is under temporary pressure from work, health, family, money, or other capacity limits while the underlying bond remains engaged.
H1.signals: Stress timing is clear; affection/interest returns when capacity improves; both people still protect the relationship and make repair efforts.
H1.counter: Distance persists across lower-stress periods or is selective to the relationship only.

H2.label: Repairable communication breakdown
H2.label_zh: 溝通出了問題，但仍可修補
H2.definition: Care and investment are still present, but conflict patterns, assumptions, avoidance, or poor repair are creating recurring disconnection.
H2.signals: Both still try; misunderstandings repeat; conversations become defensive but can eventually return; practical direction is still shared.
H2.counter: One person no longer shows curiosity, repair effort, or desire to resolve the recurring issues.

H3.label: Emotional disengagement
H3.definition: One or both people appear to be reducing emotional attention, curiosity, affection, or willingness to repair the bond.
H3.signals: Less interest in each other's inner world; relief at distance; repeated withdrawal without return; relationship maintenance feels optional.
H3.counter: Reduced warmth tracks clearly with external strain and reappears when capacity returns.

H4.label: Directional incompatibility
H4.definition: The relationship may still contain care, but major differences in future direction, values, commitment, or lifestyle are making the bond harder to sustain.
H4.signals: Same future issue repeats; major decisions stay unresolved; compromises require one person to abandon core plans.
H4.counter: Future goals remain aligned and the main problem is temporary stress or communication method.

stopping.High Evidence Band: Lead margin >=7 AND strong-primary answers >= 6 AND evidence domains >= 5
stopping.Moderate Evidence Band: Lead margin 4–6 AND minimum strong-primary/domain/stability criteria all met
stopping.Mixed / Low Evidence Band: Lead margin <4 at max, or top two remain materially supported
stopping.Deterministic Stop Rule: Before 20: continue. At/after 20: stop only if lead margin >=4, strong-primary answers >= 5, distinct positive-evidence domains >= 5, and same primary has remained #1 for last 3 answered questions. Otherwise continue until 30. At max, if margin <4 return mixed profile; never arbitrary tie-break.
stopping.Calibration Status: Production-authoring thresholds copied from approved V3.1 Deep/Standard profile; MUST pass persona simulation before RELEASE_REVIEW

resultBlueprints.Headline EN: This looks more like a relationship under pressure than a relationship that has already checked out.
resultBlueprints.Headline 中文: 這更像一段正在捱壓力的關係，而不是一段已經放棄了的關係。
resultBlueprints.We're With You EN: A relationship can look very different when both people are running on much less capacity than usual. Across your answers, the recurring clues were that the drop in warmth lines up clearly with work, family, health or money pressure and that care and interest return when the pressure eases even slightly. Taken together, the pattern is less about one dramatic moment and more about this: the relationship still appears engaged underneath a period of reduced capacity caused by pressure outside the relationship.
resultBlueprints.站在你這邊 中文: 當兩個人都比平時少了很多心力，一段關係看起來可以跟平常很不一樣。較一致的線索包括「親密感下降的時間跟工作、家庭、健康或金錢壓力很吻合」，以及「壓力一稍為減輕，關心和投入就會自然回來一些」。這些情況放在一起，較接近的解讀是：關係底下的連結仍然在，只是外在壓力暫時吃掉了大家的時間和情緒容量。
resultBlueprints.Deeper Pattern EN: Beneath the rough-phase question is a pattern question: what returns when pressure changes, and what stays broken even when it does not. Across the rough patches you described, one explanation kept carrying more weight: the relationship still appears engaged underneath a period of reduced capacity caused by pressure outside the relationship. A second pattern can still be real; the important test is what repeats across stress, repair, and future-facing moments.
resultBlueprints.更深層模式 中文: 「只是低潮還是正在散」背後，其實要看的是：壓力改變時，甚麼會回來，甚麼即使沒那麼大壓力仍然沒有好轉。你描述的幾種低潮情境裡，一個解釋一直比較有份量：關係底下的連結仍然在，只是外在壓力暫時吃掉了大家的時間和情緒容量。第二條線同樣可以是真的；更重要的是看壓力、修補和未來決定幾類情境裡，甚麼一直重複。
resultBlueprints.Professional View EN: A practical way to tell stress from deeper trouble is to watch what changes when capacity, conflict, or future decisions are tested: both people still protect the relationship with small repair efforts. This reading becomes weaker if distance continues through lower-stress periods or is selectively directed at the relationship. Use this as a working explanation of the pattern you described, not a prediction that the relationship must recover or end.

resultBlueprints.Evidence Guidance EN: The strongest part of the answer trail is where the drop in warmth lines up clearly with work, family, health or money pressure, care and interest return when the pressure eases even slightly, or both people still protect the relationship with small repair efforts. I’m also keeping the moments that point another way in view—especially anything suggesting that distance continues through lower-stress periods or is selectively directed at the relationship—because they show where this reading is less certain.

metadata.title: What Does Their Distance Actually Mean?
metadata.title_zh: 對方的疏遠究竟代表甚麼？
metadata.description: Distinguish healthy space and outside stress from emotional avoidance or a real drop in investment.
metadata.description_zh: 從對方的距離裡分清楚：對方只是需要空間、正在承受壓力、避開情感，還是投入真的在下降。

H1.label: Healthy need for space
H1.label_zh: 只是需要健康的個人空間
H1.definition: Distance is mainly a normal need for autonomy, rest, or emotional regulation that still includes clear re-engagement.
H1.signals: Asks for space directly; returns when promised; affection and plans remain intact; boundaries are respectful.
H1.counter: Space is indefinite, selectively applied, or used to avoid accountability.

H2.label: External stress
H2.label_zh: 外在壓力令對方抽不出身
H2.definition: Reduced availability is best explained by work, family, health, or other capacity pressure that affects more than just the relationship.
H2.signals: Broader stress is observable; reduced energy appears across life; still offers honest context and small signs of care.

H3.definition: Distance increases when closeness, conflict, vulnerability, or accountability becomes emotionally demanding.

resultBlueprints.Headline EN: Their distance may be space rather than rejection—especially if they reliably come back.
resultBlueprints.Headline 中文: 這份距離可能只是需要空間，不一定是拒絕你——尤其是對方每次都會回來。
resultBlueprints.We're With You EN: Distance does not always mean withdrawal; some people genuinely need space to reset and can still stay connected. Across your answers, the recurring clues were that they ask for space directly instead of disappearing without context and that they reconnect when they said they would. Taken together, the pattern is less about one dramatic moment and more about this: the distance looks more like a normal need for autonomy or regulation because it includes clear boundaries and reliable return.

resultBlueprints.Deeper Pattern EN: Distance becomes easier to read when you stop asking what one quiet period means and start asking what kind of distance keeps repeating. Across the different kinds of distance, one pattern kept showing up: the distance looks more like a normal need for autonomy or regulation because it includes clear boundaries and reliable return. resultBlueprints.Professional View EN: The most reliable way to read distance is to look at context, re-engagement, and voluntary effort rather than the silence alone: affection and future plans stay intact even while contact is lighter. This reading becomes weaker if space is indefinite, selectively applied, or repeatedly used to avoid accountability. Treat this as the best current reading of the distance pattern, not mind-reading or certainty about another person's private motives.

metadata.title: Why Am I Trying So Hard to Make This Relationship Work?
metadata.title_zh: 為甚麼我這麼努力想維持這段關係？
metadata.description: Find out whether your effort is grounded in mutual commitment—or being driven by the need to prove yourself, avoid loss, or justify everything you have already invested.
metadata.description_zh: 看看你一直努力，是因為這段關係真的值得修復，還是你在證明自己、怕失去，或捨不得已經付出的所有。

H1.label: Genuine commitment
H1.definition: The effort is mainly driven by a realistic wish to repair a relationship that still has mutual value, reciprocity, and workable problems.
H1.signals: Both contribute; effort has boundaries; repair is evidence-based; the customer can name what would make them stop trying.
H1.counter: Effort continues even when reciprocity, respect, or realistic path forward are absent.

H2.label: Proving your worth
H2.label_zh: 想證明自己值得被選擇
H2.definition: Part of the effort is about winning back approval, being chosen, or proving that the customer is worth loving.
H2.signals: Works harder after rejection; wants to become 'enough'; success is imagined as the other person finally recognizing value.
H2.counter: The customer can accept not being chosen without turning the outcome into a verdict on self-worth.

H3.label: Fear of loss
H3.definition: The work is strongly driven by how painful separation, rejection, loneliness, or replacement feels.
H3.signals: Panic at endings; self-silencing to avoid breakup; staying feels easier than facing loss even without a good path forward.
H3.counter: The customer can step away when the relationship no longer meets core needs.

H4.label: Sunk investment
H4.label_zh: 捨不得已經付出的所有
H4.definition: Time, memories, sacrifices, identity, and the story of what has already been invested make leaving feel like wasting or erasing part of life.
H4.signals: Years together dominate decisions; sacrifices justify more effort; leaving feels like making the past meaningless.
H4.counter: Future quality is judged separately from what has already been spent.

resultBlueprints.Headline EN: You may be working hard because there is still something mutual and repairable to work for.
resultBlueprints.Headline 中文: 你這麼努力，可能是因為這段關係仍然有雙方都在做的修復。
resultBlueprints.We're With You EN: Trying hard is not automatically a problem when both people are still participating in the repair. Across your answers, the recurring clues were that both people are contributing to repair rather than leaving it all to you and that you can name boundaries and conditions that would make you stop trying. Taken together, the pattern is less about one dramatic moment and more about this: your effort still looks connected to a realistic, mutual wish to repair something that has genuine value and workable problems.
resultBlueprints.站在你這邊 中文: 很努力本身不是問題，前提是修復這段關係的工作不是只有你一個人在做。較一致的線索包括「修復不是你一個人做，對方也有實際投入」，以及「你說得出自己的界線，也知道甚麼情況下會停止再努力」。這些情況放在一起，較接近的解讀是：你的努力比較像在修復一段仍然有互相價值、而且問題有機會處理的關係，而不是單方面勉強維持。
resultBlueprints.Deeper Pattern EN: The deeper question is not simply why you care so much; it is what your effort is trying to protect, prove, or avoid losing. Across the moments where you tried harder, one motive kept appearing: your effort still looks connected to a realistic, mutual wish to repair something that has genuine value and workable problems. More than one motive can drive the same effort; the useful question is which one keeps appearing across different moments of repair, fear, and choice.
resultBlueprints.更深層模式 中文: 更深的問題不只是你有多在乎，而是你的努力正在保護甚麼、證明甚麼，或者害怕失去甚麼。每次你再用力一點時，一個動機都特別容易出現：你的努力比較像在修復一段仍然有互相價值、而且問題有機會處理的關係，而不是單方面勉強維持。同一份努力可以同時有幾個原因；真正有用的是看修復、害怕和選擇幾類時刻裡，哪一個動機一直再出現。
resultBlueprints.Professional View EN: A grounded check on relationship effort is to ask whether the work is mutual, bounded, and still connected to a realistic future: effort responds to evidence of change, not only hope. This reading becomes weaker if you keep escalating effort even when reciprocity, respect or a realistic path forward are absent. Use this to understand what is driving your effort, not as an instruction to stay, leave, or prove anything to the other person.
resultBlueprints.專業／現實角度 中文: 比較落地的檢查，是看修復有沒有雙方一起做、你有沒有界線，以及這段關係前面還有沒有一條現實可走的路：「你願意繼續，是因為看得到改變證據，而不只是靠希望」。如果反而一直出現「就算互相、尊重和可行方向都已經很少，你仍然不斷再加大自己的努力」，這個解讀就需要重新評估。用它來看清甚麼正在推動你的努力，不是要求你一定留下、離開，或者再向對方證明甚麼。
resultBlueprints.Evidence Guidance EN: The evidence becomes clearest in the answers where both people are contributing to repair rather than leaving it all to you, you can name boundaries and conditions that would make you stop trying, or effort responds to evidence of change, not only hope. I’m also keeping the moments that point another way in view—especially anything suggesting that you keep escalating effort even when reciprocity, respect or a realistic path forward are absent—because they show where this reading is less certain.
resultBlueprints.答案證據指引 中文: 你答案裡最清楚的一批證據，主要是「修復不是你一個人做，對方也有實際投入」、「你說得出自己的界線，也知道甚麼情況下會停止再努力」或「你願意繼續，是因為看得到改變證據，而不只是靠希望」的情境。若同時出現「就算互相、尊重和可行方向都已經很少，你仍然不斷再加大自己的努力」這類反例，就一併一併考慮；它們正好提醒你，這個解讀在哪些地方仍未足夠穩固。
resultBlueprints.Real-Life Examples EN: In real life, this kind of effort often looks like both people are contributing to repair rather than leaving it all to you; effort responds to evidence of change, not only hope; or the relationship still offers reciprocity, respect and a realistic path forward. No single moment defines your motive; look for which of these keeps showing up when you repair, fear losing the relationship, or decide what to do next.
resultBlueprints.現實生活例子 中文: 在現實生活中，這種努力通常會像：修復不是你一個人做，對方也有實際投入；你願意繼續，是因為看得到改變證據，而不只是靠希望；或者關係裡仍然有互相、尊重和一條現實可走的路。一個時刻不能替你定義動機；看看修復、害怕失去和決定下一步時，哪幾種情況最常重複。
resultBlueprints.Watch / Try Next EN: Keep asking what evidence the relationship is giving back for the effort you are putting in. Before adding more effort, ask what has actually changed on both sides and what boundary would tell you to stop.
resultBlueprints.接下來留意／嘗試 中文: 繼續問自己：我付出的每一輪努力，這段關係實際回了甚麼證據給我。在再加更多努力之前，先看雙方實際改了甚麼，也問清楚自己到甚麼程度就不會再繼續。
resultBlueprints.Clear Wording EN: Across different moments of effort, fear, and repair, Genuine commitment appeared most consistently. That makes it a fairly clear current pattern, not a judgment about whether you should stay or leave.

resultBlueprints.Developing Wording EN: Genuine commitment explains your effort best right now, but another motive is still doing real work in the background. The result is a leading pattern, not a single-cause explanation.
resultBlueprints.發展中結果措辭 中文: 「真的想一起修復」目前最能解釋你為甚麼這麼努力，但背後仍然有另一個動機在起作用。這是領先模式，不代表所有努力只有一個原因。

metadata.title: Why Does This Person Feel So Addictive?
metadata.title_zh: 為甚麼我對這個人如此難以抽離？
metadata.description: Separate genuine connection and attraction from novelty, unpredictable attention, and the rush of feeling chosen.
metadata.description_zh: 看看這份難以抽離，來自真正的連結和吸引、新鮮刺激、忽冷忽熱的注意，還是被追逐和被選中的感覺。

H1.label: Genuine connection and attraction
H1.definition: The pull is supported by real mutual understanding, attraction, respect, and consistent enjoyment rather than intensity alone.
H1.signals: Feels both excited and at ease; connection survives ordinary periods; mutuality and respect remain when drama is low.
H1.counter: The strongest pull appears mainly during uncertainty, novelty, reunion, or validation spikes.

H2.label: Novelty and intensity
H2.definition: The relationship feels unusually compelling because it is new, emotionally charged, dramatic, or different from ordinary life.
H2.signals: High excitement; boredom when calm; fantasy expands quickly; intensity is treated as proof that the connection is special.
H2.counter: The bond remains meaningful after novelty fades and ordinary compatibility becomes visible.

H3.label: Unpredictable attention
H3.definition: Hot-cold availability may be increasing the pull because relief and reward feel especially powerful after periods of uncertainty.
H3.signals: Reunion highs; monitoring for messages; strongest desire after withdrawal; good moments erase previous distress.
H3.counter: Attention is consistent and the attraction remains strong without uncertainty.

H4.label: Validation and pursuit
H4.definition: Part of the pull comes from what winning their attention would prove about attractiveness, worth, or being chosen.
H4.signals: Competition intensifies desire; being selected matters strongly; attraction rises when the person is harder to win.
H4.counter: The customer still wants the person even when approval and competition are removed.

stopping.High Evidence Band: Lead margin >=7 AND strong-primary answers >= 5 AND evidence domains >= 4

stopping.Mixed / Low Evidence Band: Lead margin <4 at max, or top two remain materially supported
stopping.Deterministic Stop Rule: Before 15: continue. At/after 15: stop only if lead margin >=4, strong-primary answers >= 4, distinct positive-evidence domains >= 4, and same primary has remained #1 for last 3 answered questions. Otherwise continue until 18. At max, if margin <4 return mixed profile; never arbitrary tie-break.

resultBlueprints.Headline EN: The pull may be intense because the connection and attraction are genuinely strong.
resultBlueprints.Headline 中文: 這份拉力很強，可能因為你們之間真的有連結，也真的有吸引。
resultBlueprints.We're With You EN: A strong pull is not automatically a warning sign; sometimes you are genuinely drawn to someone you also feel safe with. Across your answers, the recurring clues were that you feel both excited and able to relax around them and that ordinary time together still feels meaningful after the big highs settle. Taken together, the pattern is less about one dramatic moment and more about this: the pull is supported by real mutual understanding, attraction, respect and enjoyment that still feels good when nothing dramatic is happening.
resultBlueprints.站在你這邊 中文: 很強烈的吸引不一定代表有問題；有時你是真的喜歡一個同時令你心動又可以放鬆的人。較一致的線索包括「你會心動，但同時也可以在對方面前放鬆」，以及「就算沒有很大的高潮，普通相處仍然有份量」。這些情況放在一起，較接近的解讀是：這份吸引不只靠刺激，而是有真正的互相理解、尊重和舒服感；就算沒有戲劇性事件，連結仍然站得住。
resultBlueprints.Deeper Pattern EN: The pull becomes clearer when you separate the person from the intensity, the uncertainty, and the meaning of being chosen. Across the highs, lows, and quieter moments, one source of the pull kept standing out: the pull is supported by real mutual understanding, attraction, respect and enjoyment that still feels good when nothing dramatic is happening. Another source of intensity can sit beside it; the key is what still has weight when the emotional volume changes.
resultBlueprints.更深層模式 中文: 把對方本人、強烈感、新鮮感、不確定和「被選中」的意義分開看，那份上癮感會清楚很多。高峰、低潮和平靜時刻放在一起，一個拉力來源特別突出：這份吸引不只靠刺激，而是有真正的互相理解、尊重和舒服感；就算沒有戲劇性事件，連結仍然站得住。另一種強烈來源可以同時存在；重點是當情緒音量降低之後，甚麼仍然有份量。
resultBlueprints.Professional View EN: A useful reality check is whether the bond still works when the chase, uncertainty, and emotional high are turned down: mutuality and respect remain when there is no chasing or uncertainty. This reading becomes weaker if the strongest pull appears mainly during uncertainty, novelty, reunion or validation spikes. Treat this as a way to separate sources of intensity, not as a diagnosis or proof that the connection is healthy or unhealthy.
resultBlueprints.專業／現實角度 中文: 一個很實際的檢查，是把追逐、不確定和情緒高峰調低之後，這段連結本身還有沒有份量：「沒有追逐或不確定時，互相和尊重仍然存在」。如果反而一直出現「最強的拉力主要都出現在不確定、新鮮感、重逢或突然被肯定的高峰」，這個解讀就需要重新評估。把它當成拆開不同強烈來源的方法，不是診斷，也不是證明這段連結一定健康或一定有問題。
resultBlueprints.Evidence Guidance EN: The result is anchored most strongly in the moments where you feel both excited and able to relax around them, ordinary time together still feels meaningful after the big highs settle, or mutuality and respect remain when there is no chasing or uncertainty. I’m also keeping the moments that point another way in view—especially anything suggesting that the strongest pull appears mainly during uncertainty, novelty, reunion or validation spikes—because they show where this reading is less certain.
resultBlueprints.答案證據指引 中文: 這個結果最穩的部分，來自那些出現「你會心動，但同時也可以在對方面前放鬆」、「就算沒有很大的高潮，普通相處仍然有份量」或「沒有追逐或不確定時，互相和尊重仍然存在」的情境。若同時出現「最強的拉力主要都出現在不確定、新鮮感、重逢或突然被肯定的高峰」這類反例，就一併一併考慮；它們正好提醒你，這個解讀在哪些地方仍未足夠穩固。
resultBlueprints.Real-Life Examples EN: In ordinary moments—not only the highs—this may look like you feel both excited and able to relax around them; mutuality and respect remain when there is no chasing or uncertainty; or you like who they are in everyday life, not only how intensely they make you feel. You do not need every example to match; the useful part is what still appears in both high-intensity and ordinary moments.
resultBlueprints.現實生活例子 中文: 你會心動，但同時也可以在對方面前放鬆；沒有追逐或不確定時，互相和尊重仍然存在；或者你喜歡的是對方日常真正的樣子，而不只是對方令你產生的強烈感覺。不需要每個例子都吻合；更有用的是看，情緒很高和平常相處兩邊，有甚麼都一直存在。
resultBlueprints.Watch / Try Next EN: Pay attention to how the connection feels on an ordinary, calm day when nobody is chasing. The next calm period is useful data; notice whether the connection still feels meaningful without the chase or uncertainty.
resultBlueprints.接下來留意／嘗試 中文: 特別留意一個普通而平靜、沒有人需要追誰的日子裡，你們之間的連結還剩多少。下一段平靜期會是很有用的參考；沒有追逐和不確定時，再看看這段連結本身還有沒有份量。
resultBlueprints.Clear Wording EN: Genuine connection and attraction showed up across several different kinds of attraction and uncertainty, giving it a clear lead. Treat that as the strongest current explanation, not a label that has to fit every moment.
resultBlueprints.清晰結果措辭 中文: 不同類型的吸引和不確定情境裡，「真實連結和吸引」都比較一致地出現，所以目前它最有解釋力。不需要逼自己每一刻都完全符合這個標籤。
resultBlueprints.Developing Wording EN: Genuine connection and attraction fits the pull most strongly at the moment, but another source of intensity is still clearly present. Read the result as layered rather than absolute.
resultBlueprints.發展中結果措辭 中文: 目前「真實連結和吸引」最能解釋那份拉力，但另一種強烈來源也明顯存在。這個結果比較適合分層看，不需要當成絕對答案。
resultBlueprints.Mixed Wording EN: The pull is coming from more than one place. Genuine connection and attraction explains a real part of it, and the other pattern that emerged from your answers explains another part with similar weight. Keep the result layered.
resultBlueprints.混合結果措辭 中文: 這份拉力來自不只一個地方。「真實連結和吸引」解釋了真實的一部分，另一個同樣有份量的模式也有相近份量。把結果分層看會更準確。

Prefer +2 evidence for the current primary, then include one meaningful ambiguity/counter-example and one moment that helps explain the actual secondary. Never fabricate an answer.

resultBlueprints.Safety Boundary EN: Use this as an interpretive self-reflection framework only. Do not present it as diagnosis, clinical probability, scientific certainty, or proof of another person's private intentions.

resultBlueprints.We're With You EN: Novelty and emotional intensity can make a connection feel enormous before everyday compatibility has had time to show itself. Across your answers, the recurring clues were that the connection feels most alive when something is new, dramatic or uncertain and that calm periods quickly start to feel flat or disappointing. Taken together, the pattern is less about one dramatic moment and more about this: newness, emotional charge and intensity may be doing a lot of the work of making this connection feel uniquely special.
resultBlueprints.站在你這邊 中文: 新鮮感和強烈情緒可以令一段關係很快變得很巨大，但日常合不合拍其實還未有時間看清楚。較一致的線索包括「有新鮮、戲劇性或不確定事件時，這段關係特別有生命力」，以及「一平靜下來，很快就覺得淡或不夠」。這些情況放在一起，較接近的解讀是：新鮮感、情緒刺激和強烈程度，可能替這段連結加了很多『特別』的感覺。
resultBlueprints.Deeper Pattern EN: The pull becomes clearer when you separate the person from the intensity, the uncertainty, and the meaning of being chosen. Across the highs, lows, and quieter moments, one source of the pull kept standing out: newness, emotional charge and intensity may be doing a lot of the work of making this connection feel uniquely special. Another source of intensity can sit beside it; the key is what still has weight when the emotional volume changes.
resultBlueprints.更深層模式 中文: 把對方本人、強烈感、新鮮感、不確定和「被選中」的意義分開看，那份上癮感會清楚很多。高峰、低潮和平靜時刻放在一起，一個拉力來源特別突出：新鮮感、情緒刺激和強烈程度，可能替這段連結加了很多『特別』的感覺。另一種強烈來源可以同時存在；重點是當情緒音量降低之後，甚麼仍然有份量。
resultBlueprints.Professional View EN: A useful reality check is whether the bond still works when the chase, uncertainty, and emotional high are turned down: fantasy about the future expands faster than real knowledge of each other. This reading becomes weaker if the bond remains meaningful after novelty fades and ordinary compatibility becomes visible. Treat this as a way to separate sources of intensity, not as a diagnosis or proof that the connection is healthy or unhealthy.
resultBlueprints.專業／現實角度 中文: 一個很實際的檢查，是把追逐、不確定和情緒高峰調低之後，這段連結本身還有沒有份量：「對未來的想像跑得比真正了解對方快很多」。如果反而一直出現「新鮮感退下來、普通相處和真正合不合開始清楚後，連結仍然有份量」，這個解讀就需要重新評估。把它當成拆開不同強烈來源的方法，不是診斷，也不是證明這段連結一定健康或一定有問題。
resultBlueprints.Evidence Guidance EN: The result is anchored most strongly in the moments where the connection feels most alive when something is new, dramatic or uncertain, calm periods quickly start to feel flat or disappointing, or fantasy about the future expands faster than real knowledge of each other. I’m also keeping the moments that point another way in view—especially anything suggesting that the bond remains meaningful after novelty fades and ordinary compatibility becomes visible—because they show where this reading is less certain.
resultBlueprints.答案證據指引 中文: 這個結果最穩的部分，來自那些出現「有新鮮、戲劇性或不確定事件時，這段關係特別有生命力」、「一平靜下來，很快就覺得淡或不夠」或「對未來的想像跑得比真正了解對方快很多」的情境。若同時出現「新鮮感退下來、普通相處和真正合不合開始清楚後，連結仍然有份量」這類反例，就一併一併考慮；它們正好提醒你，這個解讀在哪些地方仍未足夠穩固。
resultBlueprints.Real-Life Examples EN: In ordinary moments—not only the highs—this may look like the connection feels most alive when something is new, dramatic or uncertain; fantasy about the future expands faster than real knowledge of each other; or intensity itself starts to feel like proof that the bond must be unusually important. You do not need every example to match; the useful part is what still appears in both high-intensity and ordinary moments.
resultBlueprints.現實生活例子 中文: 有新鮮、戲劇性或不確定事件時，這段關係特別有生命力；對未來的想像跑得比真正了解對方快很多；或者感覺愈強烈，就愈容易把強烈本身當成這段關係一定很特別的證據。不需要每個例子都吻合；更有用的是看，情緒很高和平常相處兩邊，有甚麼都一直存在。
resultBlueprints.Watch / Try Next EN: Let the relationship have boring days and see whether curiosity, respect and fit survive without a high. The next calm period is useful data; notice whether the connection still feels meaningful without the chase or uncertainty.
resultBlueprints.接下來留意／嘗試 中文: 容許關係有一些悶日子，再看沒有高峰時，好奇、尊重和合拍仍不仍然存在。下一段平靜期會是很有用的參考；沒有追逐和不確定時，再看看這段連結本身還有沒有份量。
resultBlueprints.Clear Wording EN: Novelty and intensity showed up across several different kinds of attraction and uncertainty, giving it a clear lead. Treat that as the strongest current explanation, not a label that has to fit every moment.
resultBlueprints.清晰結果措辭 中文: 不同類型的吸引和不確定情境裡，「新鮮感和強烈刺激」都比較一致地出現，所以目前它最有解釋力。不需要逼自己每一刻都完全符合這個標籤。
resultBlueprints.Developing Wording EN: Novelty and intensity fits the pull most strongly at the moment, but another source of intensity is still clearly present. Read the result as layered rather than absolute.
resultBlueprints.發展中結果措辭 中文: 目前「新鮮感和強烈刺激」最能解釋那份拉力，但另一種強烈來源也明顯存在。這個結果比較適合分層看，不需要當成絕對答案。
resultBlueprints.Mixed Wording EN: The pull is coming from more than one place. Novelty and intensity explains a real part of it, and the other pattern that emerged from your answers explains another part with similar weight. Keep the result layered.
resultBlueprints.混合結果措辭 中文: 這份拉力來自不只一個地方。「新鮮感和強烈刺激」解釋了真實的一部分，另一個同樣有份量的模式也有相近份量。把結果分層看會更準確。
resultBlueprints.Evidence Selection EN: For Standard results, select 4–6 actual answered moments across distinct scenario domains (target at least 4 domains where available). resultBlueprints.更深層模式 中文: 把對方本人、強烈感、新鮮感、不確定和「被選中」的意義分開看，那份上癮感會清楚很多。高峰、低潮和平靜時刻放在一起，一個拉力來源特別突出：其中一部分強烈感，可能來自『如果我能令對方選我，這代表我夠吸引、夠重要』這種證明。另一種強烈來源可以同時存在；重點是當情緒音量降低之後，甚麼仍然有份量。
resultBlueprints.Professional View EN: A useful reality check is whether the bond still works when the chase, uncertainty, and emotional high are turned down: their difficulty to win increases the value you place on their attention. This reading becomes weaker if you still want the person when approval, competition and the thrill of winning are removed. Treat this as a way to separate sources of intensity, not as a diagnosis or proof that the connection is healthy or unhealthy.
resultBlueprints.專業／現實角度 中文: 一個很實際的檢查，是把追逐、不確定和情緒高峰調低之後，這段連結本身還有沒有份量：「對方愈難追到，他們的注意就愈顯得有價值」。如果反而一直出現「即使沒有勝負、比較和被肯定的刺激，你仍然真心想跟這個人在一起」，這個解讀就需要重新評估。把它當成拆開不同強烈來源的方法，不是診斷，也不是證明這段連結一定健康或一定有問題。
resultBlueprints.Evidence Guidance EN: The result is anchored most strongly in the moments where competition or the possibility of another person makes you want them more, being chosen feels almost as important as the actual relationship, or their difficulty to win increases the value you place on their attention. I’m also keeping the moments that point another way in view—especially anything suggesting that you still want the person when approval, competition and the thrill of winning are removed—because they show where this reading is less certain.
resultBlueprints.答案證據指引 中文: 這個結果最穩的部分，來自那些出現「一有競爭或可能出現第三者，你反而更想要對方」、「被對方選中這件事，本身幾乎跟真正相處一樣重要」或「對方愈難追到，他們的注意就愈顯得有價值」的情境。若同時出現「即使沒有勝負、比較和被肯定的刺激，你仍然真心想跟這個人在一起」這類反例，就一併一併考慮；它們正好提醒你，這個解讀在哪些地方仍未足夠穩固。
resultBlueprints.Real-Life Examples EN: In ordinary moments—not only the highs—this may look like competition or the possibility of another person makes you want them more; their difficulty to win increases the value you place on their attention; or you imagine finally securing them as a powerful confirmation of your worth. You do not need every example to match; the useful part is what still appears in both high-intensity and ordinary moments.
resultBlueprints.現實生活例子 中文: 一有競爭或可能出現第三者，你反而更想要對方；對方愈難追到，他們的注意就愈顯得有價值；或者你會想像，如果最後真的可以得到對方，好像會很有力地證明自己值得被愛。不需要每個例子都吻合；更有用的是看，情緒很高和平常相處兩邊，有甚麼都一直存在。
resultBlueprints.Watch / Try Next EN: Ask what remains attractive if nobody else is competing and their attention no longer feels like a prize. The next calm period is useful data; notice whether the connection still feels meaningful without the chase or uncertainty.
resultBlueprints.接下來留意／嘗試 中文: 可以問自己：如果沒有人跟我競爭，而對方的注意也不再像獎品，我仍然最被甚麼吸引。下一段平靜期會是很有用的參考；沒有追逐和不確定時，再看看這段連結本身還有沒有份量。
resultBlueprints.Clear Wording EN: Validation and pursuit showed up across several different kinds of attraction and uncertainty, giving it a clear lead. Treat that as the strongest current explanation, not a label that has to fit every moment.
resultBlueprints.清晰結果措辭 中文: 不同類型的吸引和不確定情境裡，「被追逐、被選中的感覺」都比較一致地出現，所以目前它最有解釋力。不需要逼自己每一刻都完全符合這個標籤。
resultBlueprints.Developing Wording EN: Validation and pursuit fits the pull most strongly at the moment, but another source of intensity is still clearly present. Read the result as layered rather than absolute.
resultBlueprints.發展中結果措辭 中文: 目前「被追逐、被選中的感覺」最能解釋那份拉力，但另一種強烈來源也明顯存在。這個結果比較適合分層看，不需要當成絕對答案。
resultBlueprints.Mixed Wording EN: The pull is coming from more than one place. Validation and pursuit explains a real part of it, and the other pattern that emerged from your answers explains another part with similar weight. Keep the result layered.
resultBlueprints.混合結果措辭 中文: 這份拉力來自不只一個地方。「被追逐、被選中的感覺」解釋了真實的一部分，另一個同樣有份量的模式也有相近份量。把結果分層看會更準確。
resultBlueprints.Evidence Selection EN: For Standard results, select 4–6 actual answered moments across distinct scenario domains (target at least 4 domains where available). Prefer +2 evidence for the current primary, then include one meaningful ambiguity/counter-example and one moment that helps explain the actual secondary. Never fabricate an answer.
resultBlueprints.證據選取規則 中文: Standard 結果選取 4–6 個顧客實際答過的證據時刻，盡量橫跨不同情境領域（資料足夠時至少 4 個）。先選目前主要模式的 +2 強證據，再加入一個有意義的模糊位／反例，以及一個能解釋實際次要模式的答案。不可捏造顧客沒有選過的答案。
resultBlueprints.Safety Boundary EN: Use this as an interpretive self-reflection framework only. Do not present it as diagnosis, clinical probability, scientific certainty, or proof of another person's private intentions.
resultBlueprints.安全措辭 中文: 這只是一個幫你整理自己答案的自我反思框架。不要把它說成診斷、臨床機率、科學定論，也不要當成已證實另一個人內心真正想法。
resultBlueprints.Secondary H1 EN: Genuine connection and attraction also matters in this result. Part of the intensity may come from what winning their attention would prove about being attractive, valuable or chosen. At the same time, the pull is supported by real mutual understanding, attraction, respect and enjoyment that still feels good when nothing dramatic is happening. The balance of your answers still puts the first reading ahead, but the other thread explains the situations that do not fit it cleanly.
resultBlueprints.次要 H1 中文: 這個結果裡，「真實連結和吸引」同樣值得保留。其中一部分強烈感，可能來自『如果我能令對方選我，這代表我夠吸引、夠重要』這種證明；同時，這份吸引不只靠刺激，而是有真正的互相理解、尊重和舒服感；就算沒有戲劇性事件，連結仍然站得住。答案的整體份量仍然令前面這個解讀領先，但另一條線把沒有完全吻合的情況補充了出來。
resultBlueprints.Secondary H2 EN: Another pattern deserves space here too: Novelty and intensity. Part of the intensity may come from what winning their attention would prove about being attractive, valuable or chosen. At the same time, newness, emotional charge and intensity may be doing a lot of the work of making this connection feel uniquely special. So this is not an either-or result: the first reading is stronger overall, and the other thread helps make sense of the exceptions.
resultBlueprints.次要 H2 中文: 還有另一條線需要一起看：「新鮮感和強烈刺激」。其中一部分強烈感，可能來自『如果我能令對方選我，這代表我夠吸引、夠重要』這種證明；同時，新鮮感、情緒刺激和強烈程度，可能替這段連結加了很多『特別』的感覺。所以這不是非黑即白。前面這個解讀較強，但另一條線幫你理解那些沒有整齊落在同一邊的情境。
resultBlueprints.Secondary H3 EN: The result also contains a meaningful Unpredictable attention thread. Part of the intensity may come from what winning their attention would prove about being attractive, valuable or chosen. At the same time, hot-and-cold attention may be strengthening the pull because relief feels unusually rewarding after uncertainty. Taken together, the first reading carries more of the answer trail, while the other thread fills in the parts that would otherwise be left unexplained.
resultBlueprints.次要 H3 中文: 答案裡也有一部分很明顯落在「忽冷忽熱的注意」。其中一部分強烈感，可能來自『如果我能令對方選我，這代表我夠吸引、夠重要』這種證明；同時，忽冷忽熱本身可能正在加強拉力，因為等過一段不確定之後重新得到注意，那種鬆一口氣會特別強。放在一起看，前面這個解讀承擔了較多答案，而另一條線補上了原本會解釋不到的部分。

metadata.title: Have They Actually Changed?
metadata.description: Look past apologies and short-term effort to see whether the underlying behavior has actually changed over time.
metadata.description_zh: 分清楚對方是真的建立了新行為，還是環境暫時變好、危機後短期補救，或核心模式其實仍然一樣。

H1.label: Sustained behavior change
H1.label_zh: 持續而主動的行為改變
H1.definition: Change is visible in repeated behavior, accountability, boundaries, and follow-through over enough time to be tested.
H1.signals: Specific ownership; consistent new behavior; change survives stress; no need for repeated reminders; repair includes impact.
H1.counter: Change depends on crisis, fear of losing the relationship, or constant monitoring.

H2.label: Situational improvement
H2.definition: Things are better mainly because the surrounding conditions changed, not necessarily because the underlying relational pattern changed.
H2.signals: Less stress, more free time, fewer triggers; old pattern has not been tested under similar pressure.
H2.counter: New behavior remains stable when the original trigger or stressor returns.

H3.label: Repair performance
H3.definition: Apologies, promises, affection, or short bursts of effort are creating hope before the deeper pattern has been demonstrated differently.
H3.signals: Strong words after conflict; gifts or attention replace accountability; plans for change are more detailed than actual follow-through.
H3.counter: Promises are modest and matched by repeated behavior over time.

H4.label: Same core pattern
H4.label_zh: 核心模式其實仍然一樣
H4.definition: The surface presentation may have changed, but the same underlying boundary, effort, honesty, or conflict pattern keeps returning.
H4.signals: Different excuse, same impact; old cycle reappears under pressure; customer again carries repair or lowers standards.
H4.counter: Old triggers now produce a meaningfully different response and sustained repair.

stopping.High Evidence Band: Lead margin >=7 AND strong-primary answers >= 5 AND evidence domains >= 4
stopping.Moderate Evidence Band: Lead margin 4–6 AND minimum strong-primary/domain/stability criteria all met
stopping.Mixed / Low Evidence Band: Lead margin <4 at max, or top two remain materially supported
stopping.Deterministic Stop Rule: Before 15: continue. At/after 15: stop only if lead margin >=4, strong-primary answers >= 4, distinct positive-evidence domains >= 4, and same primary has remained #1 for last 3 answered questions. Otherwise continue until 18. At max, if margin <4 return mixed profile; never arbitrary tie-break.
stopping.Calibration Status: Production-authoring thresholds copied from approved V3.1 Deep/Standard profile; MUST pass persona simulation before RELEASE_REVIEW

resultBlueprints.主要模式中文: 持續而主動的行為改變
resultBlueprints.Headline EN: The strongest evidence points to change that is becoming part of their normal behavior.
resultBlueprints.Headline 中文: 最有份量的證據顯示，改變正在慢慢變成對方平常的做法。
resultBlueprints.We're With You EN: Real change can feel almost boring compared with promises: it shows up as the same better behaviour again and again. Across your answers, the recurring clues were that they take specific ownership without needing you to script the apology and that new behaviour repeats over time without constant reminders. Taken together, the pattern is less about one dramatic moment and more about this: the strongest evidence is repeated, self-initiated behaviour that looks different over time and still holds when the old trigger returns.
resultBlueprints.站在你這邊 中文: 真正的改變通常沒有承諾那麼戲劇化，它更像同一個更好的做法，一次又一次自己出現。較一致的線索包括「對方會具體承認自己的部分，不需要你告訴對方應該如何道歉」，以及「新的做法會重複出現，而且不用你不停提醒」。這些情況放在一起，較接近的解讀是：最有份量的證據，是對方自己主動建立了新的做法，而且維持了一段時間；舊壓力再出現時，新的行為仍然站得住。
resultBlueprints.Deeper Pattern EN: Change is easier to judge when you separate strong emotion from what actually repeats after the crisis has passed. Across promises, calm periods, and old triggers, one reading kept holding up best: the strongest evidence is repeated, self-initiated behaviour that looks different over time and still holds when the old trigger returns. Another explanation can still matter; what counts is which pattern survives comparable stress and old triggers over time.
resultBlueprints.更深層模式 中文: 要判斷改變，最有用的是把危機當下的強烈情緒，和事情過後真正反覆出現的行為分開。承諾、平靜期和舊觸發點放在一起，一個解讀最能站得住：最有份量的證據，是對方自己主動建立了新的做法，而且維持了一段時間；舊壓力再出現時，新的行為仍然站得住。另一個解釋仍然可以有份；真正值得看的是，在相似壓力和舊觸發點再次出現時，哪個模式仍然站得住。
resultBlueprints.Professional View EN: The strongest evidence of change is behavioural: ownership, follow-through, and a different response when the old trigger returns: the change survives stress, inconvenience or the return of an old trigger. This reading becomes weaker if the improvement depends mainly on crisis, fear of losing you or constant monitoring. Use this as the best current reading of the behaviour you described, not proof that someone has permanently changed or never will.
resultBlueprints.專業／現實角度 中文: 真正有力的改變證據在行為上：有沒有承擔、之後有沒有做到，以及舊觸發點回來時反應是不是真的不同：「壓力、麻煩或舊觸發點回來時，改變仍然維持得到」。如果反而一直出現「改善主要靠危機、怕失去你，或者你一直監察和提醒才維持得到」，這個解讀就需要重新評估。可以暫時把它理解為目前最貼近你描述行為的解讀，不是證明一個人已經永久改變，或者永遠都不會改。
resultBlueprints.Evidence Guidance EN: The strongest evidence comes from the situations where they take specific ownership without needing you to script the apology, new behaviour repeats over time without constant reminders, or the change survives stress, inconvenience or the return of an old trigger. I’m also keeping the moments that point another way in view—especially anything suggesting that the improvement depends mainly on crisis, fear of losing you or constant monitoring—because they show where this reading is less certain.
resultBlueprints.答案證據指引 中文: 最有力的證據，主要來自那些出現「對方會具體承認自己的部分，不需要你告訴對方應該如何道歉」、「新的做法會重複出現，而且不用你不停提醒」或「壓力、麻煩或舊觸發點回來時，改變仍然維持得到」的情境。若同時出現「改善主要靠危機、怕失去你，或者你一直監察和提醒才維持得到」這類反例，就一併一併考慮；它們正好提醒你，這個解讀在哪些地方仍未足夠穩固。
resultBlueprints.Real-Life Examples EN: Once the crisis has passed, this pattern may show up as they take specific ownership without needing you to script the apology; the change survives stress, inconvenience or the return of an old trigger; or repair focuses on impact and follow-through, not only promises. No single good or bad moment proves change; look for which examples keep repeating when comparable pressure returns.
resultBlueprints.現實生活例子 中文: 對方會具體承認自己的部分，不需要你告訴對方應該如何道歉；壓力、麻煩或舊觸發點回來時，改變仍然維持得到；或者修復不只停在承諾，還包括理解影響和之後的跟進。一次做得好或做得差都不能證明改變；要看相似壓力再來時，哪些行為仍然反覆出現。
resultBlueprints.Watch / Try Next EN: Watch the next repeat of the old trigger; durable change should show up without you having to manage it. Let the next difficult trigger be the test—not another promise. Watch what happens without reminders, pressure, or fear of losing you.
resultBlueprints.接下來留意／嘗試 中文: 等舊問題下一次再出現時看清楚：真正穩定的改變，不應該每次都要由你管理才發生。下一次舊觸發點真正回來時，再把它當成測試；比起另一個承諾，更值得看對方不用提醒、壓力或怕失去你時會怎樣做。
resultBlueprints.Clear Wording EN: Across promises, stress, repair, and old triggers, Sustained behavior change came through most consistently. That makes it the clearest current reading, while later behaviour can still strengthen or weaken it.
resultBlueprints.清晰結果措辭 中文: 承諾、壓力、修復和舊觸發點幾類情境裡，「持續而主動的行為改變」都最穩定地出現。現階段可以先把它放在前面，但之後的行為仍然可以令這個判斷加強或轉弱。
resultBlueprints.Developing Wording EN: Sustained behavior change is the strongest current reading, but another pattern still explains some important situations. More time under comparable pressure would make the picture clearer.

resultBlueprints.證據選取規則 中文: Standard 結果選取 4–6 個顧客實際答過的證據時刻，盡量橫跨不同情境領域（資料足夠時至少 4 個）。先選目前主要模式的 +2 強證據，再加入一個有意義的模糊位／反例，以及一個能解釋實際次要模式的答案。不可捏造顧客沒有選過的答案。
resultBlueprints.Safety Boundary EN: Use this as an interpretive self-reflection framework only. Do not present it as diagnosis, clinical probability, scientific certainty, or proof of another person's private intentions.
resultBlueprints.安全措辭 中文: 這只是一個幫你整理自己答案的自我反思框架。不要把它說成診斷、臨床機率、科學定論，也不要當成已證實另一個人內心真正想法。
resultBlueprints.Secondary H1 EN: There is also a second thread here: Sustained behavior change. The repair looks convincing in the immediate aftermath of a problem, but words, affection or effort have not yet become a stable everyday pattern. At the same time, the strongest evidence is repeated, self-initiated behaviour that looks different over time and still holds when the old trigger returns. Overall, the first pattern appears more consistently in your answers, while the other thread explains the moments that pull in another direction.
resultBlueprints.次要 H1 中文: 另外，「持續而主動的行為改變」也有份。危機之後的補救看起來很有誠意，但道歉、親密或努力還未真正變成日常而穩定的新做法；同時，最有份量的證據，是對方自己主動建立了新的做法，而且維持了一段時間；舊壓力再出現時，新的行為仍然站得住。整體看，前面這個解讀在你的答案裡出現得更穩定；另一條線則解釋了那些朝另一個方向走的時刻。
resultBlueprints.Secondary H2 EN: Situational improvement also matters in this result. The repair looks convincing in the immediate aftermath of a problem, but words, affection or effort have not yet become a stable everyday pattern. At the same time, things may genuinely be easier now because the surrounding conditions improved, while the old relational pattern has not yet been fully tested. The balance of your answers still puts the first reading ahead, but the other thread explains the situations that do not fit it cleanly.
resultBlueprints.次要 H2 中文: 這個結果裡，「只是環境變好了」同樣值得保留。危機之後的補救看起來很有誠意，但道歉、親密或努力還未真正變成日常而穩定的新做法；同時，現在可能真的好相處了，但其中一部分是環境變得容易；舊模式到底改了沒有，可能還未真正經過同類壓力測試。答案的整體份量仍然令前面這個解讀領先，但另一條線把沒有完全吻合的情況補充了出來。
resultBlueprints.Secondary H3 EN: N/A — this is the primary pattern.
resultBlueprints.次要 H3 中文: 不適用——這就是主要模式。
resultBlueprints.Secondary H4 EN: The result also contains a meaningful Same core pattern thread. The repair looks convincing in the immediate aftermath of a problem, but words, affection or effort have not yet become a stable everyday pattern. At the same time, the presentation may have improved, but the same underlying pattern around effort, honesty, boundaries or conflict keeps returning. Taken together, the first reading carries more of the answer trail, while the other thread fills in the parts that would otherwise be left unexplained.
resultBlueprints.次要 H4 中文: 答案裡也有一部分很明顯落在「核心模式其實仍然一樣」。危機之後的補救看起來很有誠意，但道歉、親密或努力還未真正變成日常而穩定的新做法；同時，表面做法可能比以前好，但投入、坦白、界線或衝突底下那個核心循環仍然一次又一次回來。放在一起看，前面這個解讀承擔了較多答案，而另一條線補上了原本會解釋不到的部分。

resultBlueprints.主要模式中文: 核心模式其實仍然一樣
resultBlueprints.Headline EN: The same core pattern is still showing up, even if the apology or presentation has improved.
resultBlueprints.Headline 中文: 核心模式仍然在重複，只是道歉或表面做法比以前好了。
resultBlueprints.We're With You EN: A pattern can look different on the surface and still leave you carrying the same hurt, responsibility, or boundary problem. Across your answers, the recurring clues were that the excuse changes but the impact on you stays strikingly similar and that the old cycle reappears once pressure or conflict returns. Taken together, the pattern is less about one dramatic moment and more about this: the presentation may have improved, but the same underlying pattern around effort, honesty, boundaries or conflict keeps returning.
resultBlueprints.站在你這邊 中文: 表面做法可以變了，但如果你最後仍然承受同一種傷害、責任或界線問題，核心模式可能其實沒有走遠。較一致的線索包括「解釋換了，但最後落在你身上的影響跟以前很相似」，以及「一有壓力或衝突，舊循環又重新出現」。這些情況放在一起，較接近的解讀是：表面做法可能比以前好，但投入、坦白、界線或衝突底下那個核心循環仍然一次又一次回來。
resultBlueprints.Deeper Pattern EN: Change is easier to judge when you separate strong emotion from what actually repeats after the crisis has passed. Across promises, calm periods, and old triggers, one reading kept holding up best: the presentation may have improved, but the same underlying pattern around effort, honesty, boundaries or conflict keeps returning. Another explanation can still matter; what counts is which pattern survives comparable stress and old triggers over time.
resultBlueprints.更深層模式 中文: 要判斷改變，最有用的是把危機當下的強烈情緒，和事情過後真正反覆出現的行為分開。承諾、平靜期和舊觸發點放在一起，一個解讀最能站得住：表面做法可能比以前好，但投入、坦白、界線或衝突底下那個核心循環仍然一次又一次回來。另一個解釋仍然可以有份；真正值得看的是，在相似壓力和舊觸發點再次出現時，哪個模式仍然站得住。
resultBlueprints.Professional View EN: The strongest evidence of change is behavioural: ownership, follow-through, and a different response when the old trigger returns: you are again carrying most of the repair or lowering the same boundary. This reading becomes weaker if the old trigger now produces a meaningfully different response followed by sustained repair. Use this as the best current reading of the behaviour you described, not proof that someone has permanently changed or never will.
resultBlueprints.專業／現實角度 中文: 真正有力的改變證據在行為上：有沒有承擔、之後有沒有做到，以及舊觸發點回來時反應是不是真的不同：「最後又是你承擔大部分修復，或者再次放低同一條界線」。如果反而一直出現「同一個舊觸發點再出現時，對方真的做出了明顯不同的回應，而且之後有持續修復」，這個解讀就需要重新評估。可以暫時把它理解為目前最貼近你描述行為的解讀，不是證明一個人已經永久改變，或者永遠都不會改。
resultBlueprints.Evidence Guidance EN: The strongest evidence comes from the situations where the excuse changes but the impact on you stays strikingly similar, the old cycle reappears once pressure or conflict returns, or you are again carrying most of the repair or lowering the same boundary. I’m also keeping the moments that point another way in view—especially anything suggesting that the old trigger now produces a meaningfully different response followed by sustained repair—because they show where this reading is less certain.
resultBlueprints.答案證據指引 中文: 最有力的證據，主要來自那些出現「解釋換了，但最後落在你身上的影響跟以前很相似」、「一有壓力或衝突，舊循環又重新出現」或「最後又是你承擔大部分修復，或者再次放低同一條界線」的情境。若同時出現「同一個舊觸發點再出現時，對方真的做出了明顯不同的回應，而且之後有持續修復」這類反例，就一併一併考慮；它們正好提醒你，這個解讀在哪些地方仍未足夠穩固。
resultBlueprints.Real-Life Examples EN: Once the crisis has passed, this pattern may show up as the excuse changes but the impact on you stays strikingly similar; you are again carrying most of the repair or lowering the same boundary; or the behaviour looks different on the surface but produces the same relational outcome. No single good or bad moment proves change; look for which examples keep repeating when comparable pressure returns.
resultBlueprints.現實生活例子 中文: 解釋換了，但最後落在你身上的影響跟以前很相似；最後又是你承擔大部分修復，或者再次放低同一條界線；或者表面行為有些不同，但關係最後仍然走回同一個結果。一次做得好或做得差都不能證明改變；要看相似壓力再來時，哪些行為仍然反覆出現。
resultBlueprints.Watch / Try Next EN: Compare the impact, not only the apology: when the same kind of problem returns, does your actual experience change. Let the next difficult trigger be the test—not another promise. Watch what happens without reminders, pressure, or fear of losing you.
resultBlueprints.接下來留意／嘗試 中文: 不要只比較道歉說得有沒有更好，而要比較影響：同類問題再來時，你實際經歷到的結果有沒有不同。下一次舊觸發點真正回來時，再把它當成測試；比起另一個承諾，更值得看對方不用提醒、壓力或怕失去你時會怎樣做。
resultBlueprints.Clear Wording EN: Across promises, stress, repair, and old triggers, Same core pattern came through most consistently. That makes it the clearest current reading, while later behaviour can still strengthen or weaken it.
resultBlueprints.清晰結果措辭 中文: 承諾、壓力、修復和舊觸發點幾類情境裡，「核心模式其實仍然一樣」都最穩定地出現。現階段可以先把它放在前面，但之後的行為仍然可以令這個判斷加強或轉弱。
resultBlueprints.Developing Wording EN: Same core pattern is the strongest current reading, but another pattern still explains some important situations. More time under comparable pressure would make the picture clearer.
resultBlueprints.發展中結果措辭 中文: 現在最吻合的是「核心模式其實仍然一樣」，但另一個模式仍然解釋了一些重要情況。等相似壓力再真正出現，畫面會更清楚。
resultBlueprints.Mixed Wording EN: The evidence does not support one clean verdict on change. Same core pattern fits part of the pattern, while the other pattern that emerged from your answers also explains important moments. Both need to stay visible.
resultBlueprints.混合結果措辭 中文: 現有證據不足以支持一個乾淨的『已改／未改』結論。「核心模式其實仍然一樣」符合一部分，另一個同樣有份量的模式也解釋了重要時刻。兩邊都需要保留。
